docs.title: Security
docs.text: Security configuration for production Cognibrain deployments.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Cognibrain supports multiple authentication methods:

docs.title: API Key
docs.text:
The simplest auth method for local and private single-developer deployments:

export MEMORY_API_KEY="your-secure-random-key"

Clients authenticate with:

curl -H "X-API-Key: your-key" http://localhost:8787/api/memories

Generate a strong key

openssl rand -hex 32

docs.title: JWT / OIDC
docs.text:
For network-exposed deployments with an existing identity provider:

export MEMORY_OIDC_ISSUER="https://auth.example.com"
export MEMORY_OIDC_AUDIENCE="cognibrain"

Clients authenticate with:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer your-jwt-token" http://localhost:8787/api/memories

docs.title: No Auth (Development Only)
docs.text:
The solo-dev profile disables auth by default. This is only safe for local development on a single machine.

Never run without auth in production

Any network-accessible Cognibrain instance must have authentication configured.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text: The API includes an optional JWT/OIDC verifier, API-key auth, actor scopes, and route-level RBAC for protected routes. In strict policy mode, unmatched policy checks default to deny, and deployment reviews should verify which target database is backing the runtime before enabling production traffic.

docs.title: Policy Mode
docs.text:
export MEMORY_POLICY_MODE="production"  # Default-deny for unmatched policy checks
Mode Behavior development Permissive — allows most operations without explicit policy production Strict — unmatched policy checks default to deny

docs.title: Actor Scopes
docs.text:
API keys and tokens can be scoped to specific operations:

Scope Allows read List and retrieve memories, context packs write Create, update, archive memories admin Service management, connector config, dream cycles

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
1. Never commit secrets to source control
  2. Use environment variables for API keys and tokens
  3. Use env: references in connector configs (not literal values)
  4. Rotate keys periodically

docs.title: Connector Secrets
docs.text:
Connector configurations store only references to secrets:

# Correct — references an env var
cognibrain connections add slack --token-env MEMORY_SLACK_TOKEN

# WRONG — never do this
cognibrain connections add slack --set token=xoxb-actual-secret

docs.title: Environment Variable Priority
docs.text: Source Priority CLI flags Highest Environment variables High Runtime-local config file Medium Profile defaults Lowest

docs.title: Bind Address
docs.text:
By default, Cognibrain binds to 127.0.0.1 (localhost only):

# Only accessible from the same machine (default)
export COGNIBRAIN_HOST="127.0.0.1"

# Accessible from network (use with TLS + auth)
export COGNIBRAIN_HOST="0.0.0.0"

Binding to 0.0.0.0

If you bind to all interfaces, you must configure authentication and use TLS.

docs.title: TLS
docs.text:
Cognibrain doesn't terminate TLS directly. Use a reverse proxy:

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name cognibrain.internal.example.com;

    ssl_certificate /etc/ssl/certs/cognibrain.crt;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/ssl/private/cognibrain.key;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8787;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }
}

docs.title: Memory Content
docs.text:
• Memories may contain sensitive engineering knowledge
  • Access is controlled by authentication and policy mode
  • Consider network isolation for deployments with sensitive content

docs.title: Connector Data
docs.text:
• Connector tokens are stored as env: references, never as plaintext
  • CLI and API inspection paths expose connector configs in redacted form
  • Live smoke tests are opt-in and never run automatically

docs.title: Backup Security
docs.text:
• Encrypt database backups at rest
  • Restrict access to backup storage
  • Include backup verification in your security review

docs.title: Recommended Production Posture
docs.text:
# Authentication
export MEMORY_API_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"

# Or OIDC when an identity provider is required
export MEMORY_OIDC_ISSUER="https://auth.company.com"
export MEMORY_OIDC_AUDIENCE="cognibrain"

# Strict policy
export MEMORY_POLICY_MODE="production"

# Database-backed persistence
export MEMORY_POSTGRES_URL="postgresql://cognibrain:secret@db:5432/cognibrain"

# Localhost-only binding (reverse proxy handles external access)
export COGNIBRAIN_HOST="127.0.0.1"

docs.title: Security Checklist
docs.text:
• Authentication configured (API key or OIDC)
  • Policy mode set to production
  • TLS configured (via reverse proxy)
  • Bind address restricted to localhost
  • Connector secrets in environment variables
  • Database credentials not in source control
  • Backup encryption enabled
  • Access logs enabled
  • Regular key rotation scheduled

docs.title: Self-Hosting
docs.text: Cognibrain is designed to run as a self-hosted service controlled entirely by the CLI. This guide covers persistent single-developer deployment on your own machine or private infrastructure.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A production Cognibrain deployment consists of:

  1. The Cognibrain daemon — HTTP API serving all surfaces
  2. A storage backend — SQLite or PostgreSQL
  3. A service manager — keeps the daemon running across reboots
  4. (Optional) Connectors — configured integrations to external systems

docs.title: Quick Production Setup
docs.text:
# Install
npm i -g @cognilabz/cognibrain

# Initialize the single-developer profile
cognibrain init --profile solo-dev --yes

# Configure storage
export MEMORY_POSTGRES_URL="postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/cognibrain"
cognibrain connections add storage-postgres --url-env MEMORY_POSTGRES_URL

# Configure auth
export MEMORY_API_KEY="your-secure-api-key"
export MEMORY_POLICY_MODE="production"

# Install as service
cognibrain service install --activate

# Verify
cognibrain status
cognibrain doctor --fix

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
cognibrain service plan              # Preview what will be installed
cognibrain service install --activate # Install and start

docs.title: Supported Managers
docs.text: Platform Default System-wide Linux systemd user service --system for system service macOS launchd LaunchAgent --system for LaunchDaemon Windows Task Scheduler Startup task

docs.title: Operational Commands
docs.text:
cognibrain service status     # Is it running?
cognibrain service logs       # View recent logs
cognibrain service restart    # Restart after config change
cognibrain service uninstall --deactivate  # Remove completely

docs.title: PostgreSQL (Recommended for Production)
docs.text:
# Set the connection URL
export MEMORY_POSTGRES_URL="postgresql://cognibrain:secret@db.internal:5432/cognibrain"

# Add the storage connector
cognibrain connections add storage-postgres --url-env MEMORY_POSTGRES_URL

# Verify connectivity
npm run internal -- verify:postgres

Connection pooling

For high-throughput deployments, place a connection pooler (PgBouncer, pgpool) between Cognibrain and PostgreSQL.

docs.title: SQLite (Single-Machine)
docs.text:
For single-machine deployments that don't need PostgreSQL:

cognibrain connections add storage-sqlite

SQLite storage lives at .cognibrain/cognibrain.db by default.

docs.title: Remote Single-Developer Deployment
docs.text:
For one developer using Cognibrain from their workstation, agent shells, and private automation:

graph TB
    subgraph "Developer Surfaces"
        D1[Workstation Agent]
        D2[Remote Shell]
        D3[CI Runner]
    end

    subgraph "Private Cognibrain Server"
        API[Cognibrain Daemon]
        PG[(PostgreSQL)]
    end

    D1 -->|HTTPS + API Key| API
    D2 -->|HTTPS + API Key| API
    D3 -->|HTTPS + API Key| API
    API --> PG

Requirements:

  • PostgreSQL storage backend
  • API key or OIDC authentication
  • One developer owns all connected agents and automation
  • Network access from developer machines to the Cognibrain host
  • TLS termination (reverse proxy recommended)

docs.title: Reverse Proxy (nginx)
docs.text:
server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name cognibrain.internal.example.com;

    ssl_certificate /etc/ssl/certs/cognibrain.crt;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/ssl/private/cognibrain.key;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8787;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    }
}

docs.title: Runtime Root
docs.text:
All runtime state lives under the runtime root:

# Default
.cognibrain/

# Override
export COGNIBRAIN_RUNTIME_ROOT=/var/lib/cognibrain
cognibrain service restart

docs.title: Automated Backups
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash
# backup-cognibrain.sh
BACKUP_DIR="/backup/cognibrain/$(date +%Y%m%d)"
mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"

# PostgreSQL
pg_dump "$MEMORY_POSTGRES_URL" > "$BACKUP_DIR/cognibrain.sql"

# Runtime config (non-secret)
cp -r /var/lib/cognibrain/config.json "$BACKUP_DIR/"

docs.title: Restore
docs.text:
psql "$MEMORY_POSTGRES_URL" < backup/cognibrain.sql
cognibrain service restart
cognibrain doctor --fix

docs.title: Smoke Test
docs.text:
After any deployment:

cognibrain status
cognibrain doctor --fix
cognibrain connections doctor
cognibrain health --json

For package maintainers:

npm run verify:selfhosted

docs.title: cognibrain init
docs.text:
Initialize Cognibrain in a project directory.

cognibrain init [options]

docs.title: Custom Agent Loop
docs.text:
from cognibrain_client import CognibrainClient

client = CognibrainClient(api_key="dev-secret")

def agent_step(task: str, action: str):
    # Pre-action
    context = client.get_context(task=task)
    guard = client.guard(action=action)

    if not guard["allowed"]:
        return {"blocked": True, "reason": guard["warnings"]}

    # Execute action
    result = execute(action)

    # Post-action
    client.record_outcome(command=action, exit_code=result.exit_code)
    return {"blocked": False, "result": result}

docs.title: Harness SDK
docs.text:
For non-MCP agent runtimes that need programmatic lifecycle access:

import { CognibrainHarnessSdk } from "@cognilabz/cognibrain/sdk/typescript/harness";

const harness = new CognibrainHarnessSdk({
  baseUrl: "http://localhost:8787",
  apiKey: process.env.MEMORY_API_KEY,
});

// Before work
const context = await harness.getContext({ task: "fix auth" });

// Before risky action
const guard = await harness.checkGuard({ action: "npm test" });

// After work
await harness.recordOutcome({ command: "npm test", exitCode: 0 });
await harness.recordPatchEvidence({ task: "fix auth", files: ["src/auth.ts"] });

// End session
await harness.endSession({ runDreamIfDue: true });

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
import { CognibrainClient, CognibrainError } from "@cognilabz/cognibrain/sdk/typescript/client";

try {
  await client.memories.add({ content: "test" });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof CognibrainError) {
    console.error(`Cognibrain error [${error.code}]: ${error.message}`);
  }
}

docs.text:

}

interface PatchEvidence {
